title: Pro-étale and étale ℓ-cohomological dimensions agree
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a qcqs scheme $S$, a qcqs morphism $g\colon X\to Y$, and an integer $c\geq0$, using the scheme conventions of [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. All coefficient sheaves are abelian. Use the local $\ell$-power torsion convention of [sk-def-cd]: for $A[\ell^r]=\ker(\ell^r:A\to A)$, the canonical sheaf map $\varinjlim_{r\geq0}A[\ell^r]\to A$ is an isomorphism. Thus a section need only be killed by a power of $\ell$ locally on its site object, with no uniform exponent. The dimensions $\operatorname{cd}_\ell(S)$ and $\operatorname{cd}_\ell(g)$, the degree range $q\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$, and the suprema in $\mathbf Z_{\geq0}\cup\{+\infty\}$ (empty supremum $0$) are as in [sk-def-cd]. Classical has the meaning of [sk-def-pe-classical-definition]; the small sites and comparison morphisms $\nu$ are those of [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. The étale cohomology and direct-image notation is that of [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology] and [def-weil-pbc-direct-image].

1. For an abelian sheaf $F_0$ on $S_{\Et}$ and a classical sheaf $F\cong\nu_S^*F_0$ on $S_{\Proet}$, the sheaf $F$ is $\ell$-power torsion if and only if $F_0$ is.
2. $\operatorname{cd}_\ell(S)=\sup\{q:H^q(S_{\Et},F_0)\neq0\text{ for some }\ell\text{-power torsion sheaf }F_0\text{ on }S_{\Et}\}$.
3. $\operatorname{cd}_\ell(g)=\sup\{q:R^qg_{\Et,*}F_0\neq0\text{ for some }\ell\text{-power torsion sheaf }F_0\text{ on }X_{\Et}\}$.
4. If $\operatorname{cd}_{\rm tor}(S)\leq c$ in the sense of [def-sc-etale-torsion-cd], then $\operatorname{cd}_\ell(S)\leq c$.

proof.text: Use the existing comparison adjunction on AddCommGrpCat directly. Its inverse image is additive, preserves finite limits and all colimits, and is fully faithful by the generic Grothendieck-abelian unit theorem. The private torsion_transport lemma constructs the natural isomorphism between the images of the annihilator kernels and the annihilator kernels of an isomorphic target. Kernel uniqueness proves compatibility with the transition maps and the canonical cocones. The canonical colimit map is invertible exactly when its cocone is colimiting. Transport along the cocone isomorphism and preservation/reflection of colimits proves the torsion equivalence.
Apply cohomologicalDimension_eq_etaleCohomologicalDimension from the already stated sk-def-cd module. It has exactly clause (2), with the same prime and qcqs scheme hypotheses.
Apply relativeCohomologicalDimension_eq_etale from the already stated sk-def-cd module. Its right side is exactly the supremum in clause (3), and it requires only that the morphism is qcqs.

For an ell-power torsion etale sheaf, its annihilator cocone is colimiting. Apply a geometric stalk, which preserves colimits. Concrete.isColimit_exists_rep gives a representative of each germ in one annihilator kernel. Applying the additive stalk functor to kernel.condition shows that the germ is killed by ell^r, a positive integer. The already proved local-torsion/geometric-stalk characterization Scheme.isTorsion_iff_isAddTorsion_sheafFiber therefore gives F.IsTorsion. Apply HasTorsionEtaleCohomologicalDimensionLE in each degree n>c and convert Subsingleton to IsZero. Thus every nonvanishing degree n is at most c. Rewrite by clause (2) and apply sSup_le; the empty case is included.
